title: Penetration of avian and human influenza A viruses through mucus gel networks in vitro.
abstract: Abstract Influenza A viruses (IAVs) remain a public-health concern because of their continuous evolution and zoonotic transmission. Respiratory mucus is the first extracellular barrier encountered by inhaled viruses, yet standardized approaches for studying influenza virus passage through mucus and the infectivity of transferred virus populations remain limited. Here, we established an in vitro virus–mucus penetration assay to analyze IAV interactions with standardized mucin-containing matrices. We used mucus from human Calu-3 airway epithelial cells cultured under air–liquid interface conditions and bovine submaxillary mucin as surrogate matrices. Preparations were normalized by total protein and characterized using biochemical and biophysical methods. We compared a human seasonal H1N1pdm virus with a highly-pathogenic avian H5N1 virus. Viral genome transfer was quantified by RT-qPCR, while retained infectivity was assessed in susceptible cells. Both mucin-containing matrices restricted viral passage compared with control solutions. Viral RNA transfer and retained infectivity varied by matrix and virus, although no statistically significant difference between H1N1pdm and H5N1 was detected within either matrix. Together, these results establish a framework integrating mucus characterization with complementary measurements of viral transfer and infectivity. This approach provides a basis for investigating influenza virus–mucus interactions under controlled conditions and can be extended to other IAV strains and physiologically relevant mucus sources.

elements_zh.main_results: 与对照溶液相比,两种含有粘蛋白的基质都限制了病毒的通过。病毒 RNA 转移和保留感染性因基质和病毒而异,但在任一基质内均未检测到 H1N1pdm 和 H5N1 之间存在统计学上的显着差异。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些结果建立了一个将粘液特征与病毒转移和感染性的补充测量相结合的框架。该方法为在受控条件下研究流感病毒与粘液相互作用提供了基础。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为改进的 监测 和流感病毒诊断方法的开发提供信息,并指导通过粘液针对病毒 传播 的干预措施的设计。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的结果基于体外模型,可能无法完全代表体内条件。由于受控实验设置和缺乏临床数据,证据强度中等。

abstract_zh: 摘要 甲型流感病毒 (IAV) 由于其连续的 进化 和人畜共患的 传播 仍然是一个公共卫生问题。呼吸道粘液是吸入病毒遇到的第一个细胞外屏障,但研究流感病毒通过粘液的传播和转移病毒群体的感染性的标准化方法仍然有限。在这里,我们建立了体外病毒-粘液渗透测定来分析 IAV 与标准化含粘蛋白基质的相互作用。我们使用在气液界面条件下培养的人 Calu-3 气道上皮细胞的粘液和牛颌下粘蛋白作为替代基质。通过总蛋白对制剂进行标准化,并使用生化和生物物理方法进行表征。我们将人类季节性 H1N1pdm 病毒与高致病性禽 H5N1 病毒进行了比较。通过 RT-qPCR 对病毒 基因组 转移进行定量,同时评估易感细胞中保留的感染性。与对照溶液相比,两种含有粘蛋白的基质都限制了病毒的通过。病毒 RNA 转移和保留感染性因基质和病毒而异,但在任一基质内均未检测到 H1N1pdm 和 H5N1 之间存在统计学上的显着差异。这些结果共同建立了一个框架,将粘液表征与病毒传播和感染性的补充测量相结合。该方法为在受控条件下研究流感病毒-粘液相互作用提供了基础,并且可以扩展到其他 IAV 毒株和生理相关的粘液来源。

title: People With Influenza Requiring ICU Admission During the 2025-2026 Season, Marked by the Emergence of Influenza A(H3N2) Subclade K: A French Prospective Nationwide Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Intense influenza activity has been reported alongside the emergence of influenza A(H3N2) subclade K. While epidemiological studies have reported heterogeneous findings regarding public health impact, data remain lacking on its impact on clinical phenotype of people requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission. METHODS: Prospective, multicenter, observational SEVARVIR cohort study including people admitted in 42 French ICUs with laboratory-confirmed influenza infection during the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 seasons. Primary end point was day-28 mortality. RESULTS: Seven hundred twenty-six people were admitted for influenza in 2024-2025 (n = 360) and 2025-2026 (n = 366). In 2025-2026, influenza subtype was available for 265 people; 49% (n = 129) had A(H1N1)pdm09 and 51% (n = 136) had A(H3N2) subtype infection. Among the 40 people with A(H3N2) infection for whom whole-genome sequencing was available, 33 (82.5%) belonged to subclade K. In multivariable Cox analysis of the 2025-2026 season, age (adjusted hazard ratio, aHR = 1.04 [1.01;1.09]; P = .015), Clinical Frailty Scale (aHR = 1.59 [1.28;1.98]; P < .001), and sequential organ failure assessment score (aHR = 1.15 [1.05;1.26]; P = .003) were associated with an increased risk of death. In the 2024-2025/2025-2026 seasons or 2025-2026 season alone, influenza subtype was not associated with a significant risk of day-28 mortality. Phylogenetic analyses from our ICU cohort together with 600 contextual sequences from community-acquired influenza cases collected during the period showed no clustering according to severity. CONCLUSIONS: There was no evidence of an increased risk of death among critically ill people with influenza during the 2025-2026 season, despite the emergence of influenza A(H3N2) subclade K. TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT05162508.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 据报道,随着流感 甲型H3N2流感病毒 K 亚支的出现,流感活动也随之加剧。该研究旨在调查其对需要入住 ICU 的患者临床表型的影响。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项前瞻性、多中心、观察性 SEVARVIR 队列研究 研究在 42 个法国 ICU 中进行,其中包括 2024-2025 年和 2025-2026 年季节期间因实验室确诊流感感染入院的患者。总计726人,其中2024-2025赛季360人,2025-2026赛季366人。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究包括第 28 天 死亡率 的主要终点。对 40 名 甲型H3N2流感病毒 感染者进行了全 基因组 测序,并使用来自社区获得性流感病例的 600 个背景序列进行了系统发育分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 仅在 2025-2026 年季节,流感亚型与第 28 天 死亡率 的显着风险无关。在 40 名 甲型H3N2流感病毒 感染者中,33 人(82.5%)属于 K 亚支。系统发育分析显示,没有根据严重程度进行聚类。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出的结论是,尽管出现了流感 甲型H3N2流感病毒 K 分支,但没有证据表明 2025-2026 年季节期间流感重症患者的死亡风险增加。这一发现很新颖,因为它直接解决了 K 分支对 ICU 结局的影响。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,流感甲型H3N2流感病毒 K亚支的出现并没有显着影响危重患者的死亡率率,这可能为未来的监测和季节性流感的公共卫生策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是观察性的,不包括对照组,这可能会限制证据的强度。然而,全 基因组 测序和系统发育分析的使用提供了一种稳健的方法学方法。

abstract_zh: 背景:在流感甲型H3N2流感病毒亚系K出现的同时,报告了强烈的流感活动。尽管流行病学研究在公共卫生影响方面报告了异质性结果,但关于其对需要重症监护病房(ICU)入院人群临床表型的影响的数据仍然缺乏。方法:一项前瞻性、多中心、观察性SEVARVIR 队列研究研究,包括在2024-2025和2025-2026季节期间在42个法国ICU中接受实验室确诊流感感染的患者。主要终点是第28天死亡率。结果:在2024-2025年(n = 360)和2025-2026年(n = 366)期间,共有726名患者因流感入院。在2025-2026年,有265名患者的流感亚型可供分析;其中49%(n = 129)为甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09亚型感染,51%(n = 136)为甲型H3N2流感病毒亚型感染。在40名接受全基因组测序的甲型H3N2流感病毒感染患者中,33名(82.5%)属于亚系K。在2025-2026年季节的多变量Cox分析中,年龄(调整后风险比,aHR = 1.04 [1.01;1.09];P = .015)、临床脆弱性量表(aHR = 1.59 [1.28;1.98];P < .001)以及序贯器官衰竭评估评分(aHR = 1.15 [1.05;1.26];P = .003)与死亡风险增加相关。在2024-2025/2025-2026年季节或仅2025-2026年季节中,流感亚型与第28天死亡率的显著风险无关联。我们的ICU 队列研究的系统发育分析,结合了600个来自同期社区获得性流感病例的上下文序列,未显示根据严重程度的聚集。结论:在2025-2026年季节,尽管出现了流感甲型H3N2流感病毒亚系K,但没有证据表明重症流感患者死亡风险增加。试验注册号:NCT05162508。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 据报道,随着流感 甲型H3N2流感病毒 K 亚支的出现,流感活动也随之加剧。该研究旨在调查其对需要入住 ICU 的患者临床表型的影响。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项前瞻性、多中心、观察性 SEVARVIR 队列研究 研究在 42 个法国 ICU 中进行,其中包括 2024-2025 年和 2025-2026 年季节期间因实验室确诊流感感染入院的患者。总计726人,其中2024-2025赛季360人,2025-2026赛季366人。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究包括第 28 天 死亡率 的主要终点。对 40 名 甲型H3N2流感病毒 感染者进行了全 基因组 测序,并使用来自社区获得性流感病例的 600 个背景序列进行了系统发育分析。
analysis_zh.main_results: 仅在 2025-2026 年季节,流感亚型与第 28 天 死亡率 的显着风险无关。在 40 名 甲型H3N2流感病毒 感染者中,33 人(82.5%)属于 K 亚支。系统发育分析显示,没有根据严重程度进行聚类。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出的结论是,尽管出现了流感 甲型H3N2流感病毒 K 分支,但没有证据表明 2025-2026 年季节期间流感重症患者的死亡风险增加。这一发现很新颖,因为它直接解决了 K 分支对 ICU 结局的影响。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,流感甲型H3N2流感病毒 K亚支的出现并没有显着影响危重患者的死亡率率,这可能为未来的监测和季节性流感的公共卫生策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是观察性的,不包括对照组,这可能会限制证据的强度。然而,全 基因组 测序和系统发育分析的使用提供了一种稳健的方法学方法。

title: Substrate Adhesion Method (SAM): Ultracentrifugation-Free Electron Microscopy of Influenza A virus (H3N2) Morphology and Disinfectant-Induced Changes.
abstract: Abstract Electron microscopy (EM) is crucial for resolving viral ultrastructure, but conventional ultracentrifugation used for sample concentration can induce structural artifacts, particularly in enveloped viruses like influenza A virus. To overcome this, we developed and validated the Substrate Adhesion Method (SAM). This simple technique bypasses ultracentrifugation by utilizing the natural adhesion of influenza A virus (H3N2) to cell culture substrates during infection, enabling effective multimodal EM (SEM, TEM, STEM) visualization of progeny virus particles without prior concentration. SAM-enabled SEM revealed a distinct topographical "wavy" pattern on H3N2 virus particle surfaces, which is interpreted as a preparation-induced artifact arising from critical point drying (CPD) shrinkage. Ultra-high-voltage electron tomography confirmed that spike-containing envelope structures contribute to this observed morphology. Thus, SAM-facilitated SEM offers wide-field morphological insights complementing TEM's high-resolution internal structural analysis. Virus particle adhesion to the substrate via SAM was significantly enhanced by infected cells, suggesting a key role for cell-associated factors in this immobilization. Furthermore, SAM's compatibility with negative staining allowed direct visualization of ethanol-induced H3N2 virus inactivation via distinct envelope deformations such as disruption and roughening. This feature makes SAM a valuable tool for direct morphological assessment of disinfectant efficacy, complementing infectivity assays. In conclusion, SAM provides a simple, rapid, artifact-mitigating approach for detailed morphological studies of H3N2 virus and antiviral agent evaluation, opening new perspectives in virological EM.

elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study designed and validated the Substrate Adhesion Method (SAM) for influenza A virus (H3N2) visualization using electron microscopy techniques, including SEM, TEM, and STEM.

elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: SAM is a valuable tool for direct morphological assessment of disinfectant efficacy, complementing infectivity assays, and opening new perspectives in virological EM.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Virus particle adhesion to the substrate via SAM was significantly enhanced by infected cells, suggesting a key role for cell-associated factors in this immobilization. title_zh: 基质粘附法 (SAM):甲型流感病毒 (H3N2) 形态和消毒剂引起的变化的无超速离心电子显微镜。
source_body_en: Abstract Electron microscopy (EM) is crucial for resolving viral ultrastructure, but conventional ultracentrifugation used for sample concentration can induce structural artifacts, particularly in enveloped viruses like influenza A virus. To overcome this, we developed and validated the Substrate Adhesion Method (SAM). This simple technique bypasses ultracentrifugation by utilizing the natural adhesion of influenza A virus (H3N2) to cell culture substrates during infection, enabling effective multimodal EM (SEM, TEM, STEM) visualization of progeny virus particles without prior concentration. SAM-enabled SEM revealed a distinct topographical "wavy" pattern on H3N2 virus particle surfaces, which is interpreted as a preparation-induced artifact arising from critical point drying (CPD) shrinkage. Ultra-high-voltage electron tomography confirmed that spike-containing envelope structures contribute to this observed morphology. Thus, SAM-facilitated SEM offers wide-field morphological insights complementing TEM's high-resolution internal structural analysis. Virus particle adhesion to the substrate via SAM was significantly enhanced by infected cells, suggesting a key role for cell-associated factors in this immobilization. Furthermore, SAM's compatibility with negative staining allowed direct visualization of ethanol-induced H3N2 virus inactivation via distinct envelope deformations such as disruption and roughening. This feature makes SAM a valuable tool for direct morphological assessment of disinfectant efficacy, complementing infectivity assays. In conclusion, SAM provides a simple, rapid, artifact-mitigating approach for detailed morphological studies of H3N2 virus and antiviral agent evaluation, opening new perspectives in virological EM.
abstract_zh: 摘要 电子显微镜 (EM) 对于解析病毒超微结构至关重要,但用于样品浓缩的传统超速离心可能会导致结构伪影,特别是在甲型流感病毒等包膜病毒中。为了克服这个问题,我们开发并验证了基材粘附方法 (SAM)。这种简单的技术利用甲型流感病毒 (H3N2) 在感染过程中对细胞培养基质的自然粘附,绕过超速离心,无需事先浓缩即可对子代病毒颗粒进行有效的多模式 EM(SEM、TEM、STEM)可视化。启用 SAM 的 SEM 揭示了 H3N2 病毒颗粒表面明显的地形“波状”图案,这被解释为由临界点干燥 (CPD) 收缩引起的制剂诱导伪影。超高压电子断层扫描证实,含有尖峰的包膜结构有助于观察到这种形态。因此,SAM 辅助的 SEM 提供了宽视场形态学见解,补充了 TEM 的高分辨率内部结构分析。受感染细胞显着增强了病毒颗粒通过 SAM 与基质的粘附,表明细胞相关因子在这种固定中发挥着关键作用。此外,SAM 与负染色的兼容性允许通过不同的包膜变形(例如破坏和粗糙化)直接可视化乙醇诱导的 H3N2 病毒灭活。这一功能使 SAM 成为直接形态学评估消毒剂功效、补充感染性测定的宝贵工具。总之,SAM 为 H3N2 病毒的详细形态学研究和 抗病毒药物 药物评估提供了一种简单、快速、减少伪影的方法,为病毒学 EM 开辟了新的视角。

title: 2010 and 2013 Incidence Peaks in Narcolepsy and Idiopathic Hypersomnia Linked to Type A H1N1 and Type B Victoria Influenza Strains.
abstract: ABSTRACT Increased narcolepsy type‐1 (NT1) incidence rates were reported globally in 2010, linked to the H1N1 2009–2010 influenza pandemic and Pandemrix vaccination. A child‐specific NT1 peak was observed in Europe in 2013, further raising questions about the relationship between NT1 and influenza infections. This study analysed annual European incidence patterns of central disorders of hypersomnolence (CDH) in relation to influenza severity. All NT1 ( N = 981) and a combined group of narcolepsy type‐2 (NT2) and idiopathic hypersomnia (IH) ( N = 545) cases from eight European centers were studied from 1995 to 2019. Linear mixed models and Spearman correlations were applied to investigate the relationships between CDH incidence and the severity of preceding influenza seasons, including H1N1, H3N2, and for the Netherlands, influenza Type B Victoria and Yamagata. Peaks in NT1 incidence were present in 2010 and 2013, while a 2010 child‐specific peak was identified in NT2 and IH. Both groups showed a significantly positive correlation with H1N1 influenza severity and a negative correlation with H3N2. NT1 was also significantly associated with influenza Type B Victoria in the Netherlands, particularly in children. These findings suggest that, beyond H1N1, influenza Type B Victoria may be a novel trigger for NT1. Similar to NT1, the 2010 children peak in NT2 and IH may indicate possible immune‐related pathophysiologies linked to the 2009–2010 H1N1 pandemic. Further immunological studies are warranted to unravel the complexities of these relationships and their implications for CDH.

title: Antiviral Treatment of Human Influenza A(H5N1) Infection: Treatment Timing, Clinical Outcomes, Virological Outcomes, and Antiviral Resistance: A Systematic Review
abstract: Human influenza A(H5N1) infection remains a clinically important zoonotic disease, but evidence on antiviral effectiveness is limited by observational designs, heterogeneous treatment timing, and potentially overlapping patient populations. This systematic review synthesized evidence on antiviral regimens, treatment timing, clinical and virological outcomes, and antiviral resistance in laboratory-confirmed human A(H5N1) infection. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and ScienceDirect was conducted from database inception to 1 July 2026. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale and the JBI Case Series Checklist. The clinical and methodological characteristics varied across studies; consequently, the findings were synthesized narratively. Potential population overlap was considered when synthesizing findings across publications to avoid duplicate aggregation of patient data. Of 2,329 records identified, 22 publications were included. Oseltamivir treatment was associated with a lower hazard of death than no documented anti-influenza antiviral treatment (adjusted hazard ratio 0.51, 95% confidence interval 0.34–0.77). Treatment within 2 days showed lower odds of death, although the overall estimate was not statistically significant (adjusted odds ratio 0.17, 95% confidence interval 0.03–1.04). Among patients without respiratory failure at treatment initiation, earlier treatment was associated with lower mortality (adjusted odds ratio 0.17, 95% confidence interval 0.03–0.89). Evidence for other antivirals was limited, and one confirmed treatment-emergent H274Y neuraminidase resistance event was identified. Overall, oseltamivir, particularly when initiated early and before advanced respiratory failure, was associated with improved clinical outcomes, although causal inference remains limited by confounding, heterogeneity, and potentially overlapping study populations.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review evaluates the effectiveness of antiviral treatment for human influenza A(H5N1) infection, focusing on treatment timing, clinical outcomes, virological outcomes, and antiviral resistance. The review included 22 publications identified through a search of PubMed, Scopus, and ScienceDirect up to 1 July 2026. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale and the JBI Case Series Checklist. The findings were synthesized narratively due to variability in study designs and populations. Oseltamivir treatment was associated with a lower hazard of death compared to no treatment, with early initiation showing improved outcomes. The review highlights the need for further research to clarify the role of antivirals in A(H5N1) treatment and to address methodological limitations.

title: Genomic variability in the neuraminidase gene and antiviral susceptibility of influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses isolated from hospitalized patients in Shiraz, Iran (2023–2024)
abstract: Abstract Background The 2009 influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 pandemic caused substantial global morbidity and mortality. Mutations in the neuraminidase (NA) gene may influence viral evolution, immune evasion, and susceptibility to neuraminidase inhibitors, highlighting the importance of continuous molecular surveillance. Methods Between November 2023 and December 2024, 300 respiratory samples were collected from patients with acute respiratory infections in Shiraz, Iran, and screened for influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 by real-time RT-PCR. Fourteen positive samples underwent full-length NA gene sequencing, amino acid substitution analysis, phylogenetic analysis, structural modeling, and molecular docking with oseltamivir and zanamivir. Phylogenetic comparison was performed using the historical pandemic reference strain A/California/07/2009 (NC_026434.1) to identify neuraminidase sequence divergence relative to the founding A(H1N1)pdm09 lineage. Results Sequence analysis identified 18 distinct amino acid substitutions in the NA gene among the 14 isolates. The most frequent substitutions were V241I and N369K (13/14, 92.9%), followed by N200S (4/14, 28.6%) and V394I (2/14, 14.3%). V241I and N369K are consistent with previously reported lineage-associated permissive substitutions in circulating A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses, whereas N386K has been associated with alteration of an N-linked glycosylation site. Screening of the NA sequences for established WHO-recognized neuraminidase inhibitor resistance-associated substitutions identified no major known resistance markers, including H275Y and I223V. Molecular docking suggested preserved predicted binding of oseltamivir and zanamivir to neuraminidase. Conclusion Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses isolated from hospitalized patients in Shiraz during 2023–2024 exhibited genetic variability in the neuraminidase gene while lacking established neuraminidase inhibitor resistance-associated substitutions. These findings provide sequence-based evidence consistent with the absence of established resistance markers among the analyzed isolates and emphasize the importance of continued molecular surveillance to monitor the emergence of clinically relevant NA mutations. Clinical Trial Registration Not applicable, as this study is observational and does not involve a clinical trial.

analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted between November 2023 and December 2024, collecting 300 respiratory samples from patients with acute respiratory infections in Shiraz, Iran, and analyzing 14 positive samples for influenza A(H1N1)pdm09.
analysis.methods: Respiratory samples were screened for influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 using real-time RT-PCR. Positive samples underwent full-length NA gene sequencing, amino acid substitution analysis, phylogenetic analysis, structural modeling, and molecular docking with oseltamivir and zanamivir.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the analyzed influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 isolates exhibited genetic variability in the NA gene but lacked established neuraminidase inhibitor resistance-associated substitutions, highlighting the need for continued molecular surveillance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide insights into the genetic evolution of influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses and their potential susceptibility to neuraminidase inhibitors, which is critical for monitoring antiviral resistance and informing public health strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is observational and limited to 14 isolates, which may restrict generalizability. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on sequence analysis and molecular docking without clinical outcome data.

A total of 300 respiratory samples were collected, and 14 were positive for the virus. The NA gene was sequenced, revealing 18 distinct amino acid substitutions. The most frequent substitutions were V241I and N369K, which are associated with permissive mutations in circulating A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses. The study emphasizes the importance of molecular surveillance to monitor the emergence of clinically relevant NA mutations. However, the small sample size and observational design limit the generalizability of the findings, resulting in moderate confidence in the evidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查 2023 年至 2024 年期间从伊朗设拉子住院患者中分离出的流感 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 病毒神经氨酸酶基因的基因组变异,以评估对 抗病毒药物 易感性和病毒 进化 的潜在影响。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2023年11月至2024年12月期间进行了一项横断面研究,收集了伊朗设拉子急性呼吸道感染患者的300份呼吸道样本,并分析了14份流感甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09阳性样本。
elements_zh.methods: 使用实时 RT-PCR 对呼吸道样本进行流感 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 筛查。阳性样本进行全长NA基因测序、氨基酸取代分析、系统发育分析、结构建模以及与奥司他韦和扎那米韦的分子对接。
elements_zh.main_results: Sequence analysis identified 18 distinct amino acid substitutions in the NA gene among the 14 isolates. The most frequent substitutions were V241I and N369K (13/14, 92.9%), followed by N200S (4/14, 28.6%) and V394I (2/14, 14.3%).
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,分析的流感 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 分离株表现出 NA 基因的遗传变异性,但缺乏已确定的神经氨酸酶抑制剂耐药性相关取代,这凸显了对持续分子 监测 的需求。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了对流感 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 病毒的 进化 基因及其对神经氨酸酶抑制剂的潜在敏感性的深入了解,这对于监测 抗病毒药物 耐药性和为公共卫生策略提供信息至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是观察性的,仅限于 14 个分离株,这可能会限制普遍性。证据是中等的,因为它基于序列分析和分子对接,没有临床结果数据。

title: The infectious unit of influenza A virus is a population of particles, not a single virion, as shown by absolute particle quantification
abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) populations are characterized by a high prevalence of non-infectious virions, with particle-to-plaque forming unit (PFU) ratios typically ranging from 10 to 1,000. While "multiplicity reactivation" -the process by which incomplete viral genomes (IVGs) establish productive infection through co-infection- has long been hypothesized, its quantitative nature has remained elusive. In this study, we utilized a digital influenza assay to achieve absolute quantification of IAV particles, allowing us to define the particle-based multiplicity of infection (pMOI) for precise evaluation. We combined this approach with a single-cell infection assay using microcompartmentalized containers and machine learning-based automated cell classification to accurately assess infection outcomes across a wide range of pMOIs. Our analysis of the A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (H1N1) revealed a count-to-plaque forming unit (PFU) ratio of approximately 400, meaning only a tiny fraction of particles possesses infectivity. Remarkably, the infection rate in single-cell infection experiments followed a sigmoidal curve and reached saturation at a pMOI of only 5 to 10. This demonstrates that under high-pMOI conditions, productive infection is predominantly driven by genome complementation among incomplete particles rather than solely by fully infectious virions. On the other hand, mathematical model analysis based on these findings suggested that the functionality of each of the eight genomic segments within a virus particle follows a stochastic process, resulting in a probability distribution for the number of functional segments per particle. This mechanism proved exceptionally robust across multiple strains despite a 20-fold variation in CTPR values. Ultimately, these findings indicate that incomplete particles are not merely biological noise but active contributors to the infection process, significantly enhancing the infectivity and evolutionary flexibility of IAV. This study will provide a more refined understanding of influenza transmission dynamics and risk assessment, particularly in environments where multiple virus particles are present within a single respiratory droplet.

title: Update to the CDC influenza A(H3) subtyping assay for improved detection of influenza A(H3N2) viruses, including subclade K viruses
abstract: ABSTRACT Influenza A(H3N2) viruses circulate globally and cause respiratory illness. The FDA-cleared CDC Human Influenza Virus Real-Time RT-PCR Influenza A (H3/H1pdm09) Subtyping assay is used to subtype seasonal influenza A viruses. However, emerging mutations in the H3 reverse primer region raised concerns about reduced assay sensitivity for contemporary circulating viruses. We updated the H3 assay by redesigning the reverse primer to target a more conserved region of the hemagglutinin gene, and incorporating minor adjustments into the forward primer and probe. Analytical sensitivity, inclusivity, and exclusivity evaluations were performed using cultured influenza viruses, synthetic RNA, and panels of non-influenza respiratory pathogens. Clinical performance was evaluated using seasonal A(H3N2) residual respiratory specimens. The updated assay (H3_v2) demonstrated analytical sensitivity comparable to or improved over the initial H3 assay, with a limit of detection of approximately 10 1.7 –10 2.1 EID 50 /mL and five copies of RNA per reaction. Improved performance was observed for viruses containing A21G with T23G, T23C, or T23A double mismatches in the reverse primer, with a measurable Ct value shift between the initial H3 and H3_v2 assay. The assay showed 100% agreement with expected results in 139 clinical specimens, and no cross-reactivity with other influenza subtypes or other respiratory pathogens. These findings indicate the updated H3_v2 assay improves sensitivity for contemporary and emerging seasonal A(H3N2) viruses while maintaining high specificity. This update ensures continued reliable detection of seasonal A(H3N2), including genetically drifted A(H3N2) viruses, such as the recently emerged A(H3N2) subclade K viruses, and supports global influenza surveillance and diagnostic preparedness. IMPORTANCE Accurate detection and subtyping of influenza A(H3N2) viruses are essential for clinical diagnostics, outbreak response, and global influenza surveillance. The emergence and fixation of mutations leading to primer mismatches in the FDA-cleared CDC A(H3) real-time RT-PCR assay raised concerns about reduced sensitivity for contemporary circulating A(H3N2) viruses. To address this, we redesigned the reverse primer and optimized additional assay components to improve detection of currently circulating seasonal A(H3N2) viruses. The updated H3_v2 assay restores and enhances sensitivity, including for viruses harboring key reverse primer mismatches, while maintaining high specificity and complete agreement with clinical specimens. This update ensures reliable detection of seasonal influenza A(H3N2) and A(H3N2) variant viruses, including recently emerged A(H3N2) subclade K viruses, and strengthens diagnostic preparedness and surveillance capacity nationally and internationally.

title_zh: 更新 CDC 甲型 (H3) 流感亚型分析,以改进流感 甲型H3N2流感病毒 病毒(包括 K 亚支病毒)的检测
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Influenza A(H3N2) viruses circulate globally and cause respiratory illness. The FDA-cleared CDC Human Influenza Virus Real-Time RT-PCR Influenza A (H3/H1pdm09) Subtyping assay is used to subtype seasonal influenza A viruses. However, emerging mutations in the H3 reverse primer region raised concerns about reduced assay sensitivity for contemporary circulating viruses. We updated the H3 assay by redesigning the reverse primer to target a more conserved region of the hemagglutinin gene, and incorporating minor adjustments into the forward primer and probe. Analytical sensitivity, inclusivity, and exclusivity evaluations were performed using cultured influenza viruses, synthetic RNA, and panels of non-influenza respiratory pathogens. Clinical performance was evaluated using seasonal A(H3N2) residual respiratory specimens. The updated assay (H3_v2) demonstrated analytical sensitivity comparable to or improved over the initial H3 assay, with a limit of detection of approximately 10 1.7 –10 2.1 EID 50 /mL and five copies of RNA per reaction. Improved performance was observed for viruses containing A21G with T23G, T23C, or T23A double mismatches in the reverse primer, with a measurable Ct value shift between the initial H3 and H3_v2 assay. The assay showed 100% agreement with expected results in 139 clinical specimens, and no cross-reactivity with other influenza subtypes or other respiratory pathogens. These findings indicate the updated H3_v2 assay improves sensitivity for contemporary and emerging seasonal A(H3N2) viruses while maintaining high specificity. This update ensures continued reliable detection of seasonal A(H3N2), including genetically drifted A(H3N2) viruses, such as the recently emerged A(H3N2) subclade K viruses, and supports global influenza surveillance and diagnostic preparedness. IMPORTANCE Accurate detection and subtyping of influenza A(H3N2) viruses are essential for clinical diagnostics, outbreak response, and global influenza surveillance. The emergence and fixation of mutations leading to primer mismatches in the FDA-cleared CDC A(H3) real-time RT-PCR assay raised concerns about reduced sensitivity for contemporary circulating A(H3N2) viruses. To address this, we redesigned the reverse primer and optimized additional assay components to improve detection of currently circulating seasonal A(H3N2) viruses. The updated H3_v2 assay restores and enhances sensitivity, including for viruses harboring key reverse primer mismatches, while maintaining high specificity and complete agreement with clinical specimens. This update ensures reliable detection of seasonal influenza A(H3N2) and A(H3N2) variant viruses, including recently emerged A(H3N2) subclade K viruses, and strengthens diagnostic preparedness and surveillance capacity nationally and internationally.
abstract_zh: 摘要 流感 甲型H3N2流感病毒 病毒在全球传播并引起呼吸道疾病。FDA 批准的 CDC 人类流感病毒实时 RT-PCR 甲型流感 (H3/H1pdm09) 亚型分析用于对 季节性流感 A 病毒进行亚型分析。然而,H3 反向引物区域中出现的 突变 引起了人们对当代流行病毒检测灵敏度降低的担忧。我们通过重新设计反向引物以针对血凝素基因的更保守区域,并对正向引物和探针进行细微调整,更新了 H3 测定。使用培养的流感病毒、合成 RNA 和非流感呼吸道病原体组进行分析敏感性、包容性和排他性评估。使用季节性 甲型H3N2流感病毒 残留呼吸道标本评估临床表现。更新后的测定 (H3_v2) 证明了分析灵敏度与初始 H3 测定相当或有所提高,检测限约为 10 1.7 –10 2.1 EID 50 /mL,每个反应有 5 个 RNA 拷贝。对于反向引物中含有 A21G 和 T23G、T23C 或 T23A 双错配的病毒,观察到性能有所改善,初始 H3 和 H3_v2 测定之间的 Ct 值发生可测量的变化。该检测结果与 139 份临床样本的预期结果 100% 一致,并且与其他流感亚型或其他呼吸道病原体没有交叉反应。这些发现表明,更新的 H3_v2 检测提高了对当代和新兴季节性 甲型H3N2流感病毒 病毒的敏感性,同时保持了高特异性。此更新可确保持续可靠地检测季节性 甲型H3N2流感病毒,包括基因漂移的 甲型H3N2流感病毒 病毒,例如最近出现的 甲型H3N2流感病毒 K 亚支病毒,并支持全球流感 监测 和诊断准备。重要性 流感 甲型H3N2流感病毒 病毒的准确检测和分型对于临床诊断、暴发 应对和全球流感 监测 至关重要。突变 的出现和固定导致 FDA 批准的 CDC A(H3) 实时 RT-PCR 检测中引物错配,引起了人们对当代流行的 甲型H3N2流感病毒 病毒敏感性降低的担忧。为了解决这个问题,我们重新设计了反向引物并优化了其他检测组件,以改善对当前流行的季节性 甲型H3N2流感病毒 病毒的检测。更新后的 H3_v2 检测恢复并增强了灵敏度,包括对具有关键反向引物错配的病毒的灵敏度,同时保持了高特异性并与临床标本完全一致。此更新确保可靠检测 季节性流感 甲型H3N2流感病毒 和 甲型H3N2流感病毒 变种病毒,包括最近出现的 甲型H3N2流感病毒 K 亚支病毒,并加强国内和国际的诊断准备和 监测 能力。

title: Computationally designed multisubtype epigraph vaccine confers broad-spectrum protection against H1 and H3 swine influenza A viruses
abstract: H1 and H3 subtype swine influenza A viruses (IAV-S) threaten global agricultural economies and pose zoonotic risks, yet conventional vaccines provide limited protection against their vast antigenic diversity. Here, we developed a multisubtype vaccine utilizing adenoviral vectors expressing computationally designed H1 and H3 epigraph hemagglutinin (HA) immunogens. In mice, this All-in-One formulation elicited balanced humoral and cellular immunity and demonstrated neutralizing breadth against diverse IAV-S isolates compared to a commercially available vaccine. The multisubtype delivery system elicited concurrent immunity and protection against both H1 and H3 subtypes. The All-in-One vaccine conferred protection against heterologous H1 and H3 challenges and did not exacerbate clinical morbidity characteristic of mismatched vaccination. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of computationally optimized and multiplexed vaccines providing broad-spectrum protection against evolving influenza viruses without compromising safety.

abstract_zh: H1 和 H3 亚型甲型猪流感病毒 (IAV-S) 威胁全球农业经济并造成人畜共患风险,但传统的 疫苗 针对其巨大的抗原多样性提供的保护有限。在这里,我们利用表达计算设计的 H1 和 H3 印记血凝素 (HA) 免疫原的腺病毒 媒介 开发了多亚型 疫苗。在小鼠中,与市售的 疫苗 相比,这种多合一配方可引发平衡的体液和细胞免疫,并表现出针对多种 IAV-S 分离株的中和广度。多亚型递送系统同时引发针对 H1 和 H3 亚型的免疫和保护。多合一 疫苗 赋予针对异源 H1 和 H3 挑战的保护作用,并且不会加剧不匹配的 疫苗接种 的临床发病特征。这些发现证明了计算优化和多重 疫苗 在不影响安全性的情况下提供针对不断变化的流感病毒的广谱保护的可行性。

title: Oxidized Cellulose Nanofiber Hydrogels for 3D Airway Spheroids and Influenza Infection Modeling
abstract: ABSTRACT Micro‐physiological systems (MPS) that recapitulate tissue architecture and immune competence are urgently needed to model respiratory viral infections and accelerate antiviral discovery. Here, we create an airway spheroid‐based MPS supported by an oxidized cellulose nanofiber (OCNF) hydrogel, which provides a hydrated, extracellular matrix (ECM) mimetic nanofibrillar microenvironment and supports stable long‐term 3D culture. Airway epithelial‐like spheroids are generated either from Calu‐3 cells alone or as immunocompetent co‐culture spheroids incorporating polarized THP‐1 macrophage‐like cells to capture epithelial‐immune crosstalk. The OCNF platform promotes rapid spheroid self‐assembly within 6 days and preserves structural integrity for ≥ 20 days, allowing longitudinal interrogation of influenza A virus replication and host innate immune responses. Notably, the model reveals that human bone marrow‐derived mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) exert potent antiviral activity, significantly reducing influenza infection through activation of interferon (IFN)‐associated pathways, including MX1, OAS1, and STAT1. Together, this OCNF hydrogel‐enabled airway spheroid MPS provides a scalable and reproducible test‐bed for mechanistic studies and preclinical evaluation of antiviral interventions and establishes an in vitro platform toward personalized patient‐relevant respiratory infection models.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to develop a micro-physiological system (MPS) that can model respiratory viral infections and support antiviral discovery by recapitulating tissue architecture and immune competence.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study created an airway spheroid-based MPS using oxidized cellulose nanofiber (OCNF) hydrogel, which supports stable long-term 3D culture and allows for longitudinal analysis of influenza A virus replication and host immune responses.
analysis.methods: Airway epithelial-like spheroids were generated from Calu-3 cells or as immunocompetent co-cultures with polarized THP-1 macrophage-like cells. The OCNF hydrogel platform enabled rapid spheroid self-assembly within 6 days and preserved structural integrity for ≥ 20 days.
analysis.main_results: The OCNF hydrogel platform allowed for the rapid self-assembly of airway spheroids within 6 days and maintained their structural integrity for at least 20 days, facilitating longitudinal study of influenza A virus replication and host immune responses.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The model demonstrated that human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) have potent antiviral activity against influenza A virus, significantly reducing infection through activation of IFN-associated pathways.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings establish an in vitro platform for preclinical evaluation of antiviral interventions and offer a scalable method for personalized respiratory infection models relevant to seasonal influenza.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro models and does not include in vivo validation, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate due to the absence of clinical data.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces an oxidized cellulose nanofiber (OCNF) hydrogel platform that supports the creation of airway spheroid-based micro-physiological systems (MPS) for modeling respiratory viral infections. The OCNF hydrogel enables rapid spheroid self-assembly within 6 days and maintains structural integrity for at least 20 days, allowing for longitudinal analysis of influenza A virus replication and host immune responses. The model reveals that human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) exhibit potent antiviral activity against influenza A virus by activating IFN-associated pathways. These findings provide a scalable and reproducible in vitro platform for preclinical evaluation of antiviral interventions and personalized respiratory infection models. However, the study is limited to in vitro models and lacks in vivo validation, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate due to the absence of clinical data.

abstract_zh: 摘要:迫切需要能够概括组织结构和免疫能力的微生理系统(MPS)来模拟呼吸道病毒感染并加速 抗病毒药物 的发现。在这里,我们创建了一种基于气道球体的 MPS,由氧化纤维素纳米纤维 (OCNF) 水凝胶支持,它提供了水合的细胞外基质 (ECM) 模拟纳米纤维微环境,并支持稳定的长期 3D 培养。气道上皮样球体可以单独由 Calu-3 细胞生成,也可以作为包含极化 THP-1 巨噬细胞样细胞的免疫活性共培养球体生成,以捕获上皮免疫串扰。OCNF 平台可在 6 天内促进球体快速自组装,并保持结构完整性 ≥ 20 天,从而允许对甲型流感病毒复制和 宿主 固有 免疫应答 进行纵向询问。值得注意的是,该模型揭示人骨髓间充质干细胞 (MSC) 发挥有效的 抗病毒药物 活性,通过激活干扰素 (IFN) 相关途径(包括 MX1、OAS1 和 STAT1)显着减少流感感染。总之,这种支持 OCNF 水凝胶的气道球体 MPS 为 抗病毒药物 干预措施的机械研究和临床前评估提供了可扩展且可重复的测试平台,并建立了一个针对个性化患者相关呼吸道感染模型的体外平台。

title: Ethyl caffeate restores BNIP3L-dependent mitophagy and mitochondrial function to ameliorate influenza A virus-induced lung injury
abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) infection induces severe lung injury characterized by excessive inflammation and mitochondrial dysfunction, in which impaired mitochondrial clearance plays a crucial role. Ethyl caffeate (EC), a bioactive phenolic compound of dietary origin, exhibits potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. However, its protective role against IAV-triggered lung damage and mitochondrial quality control dysfunction remains poorly defined. In this study, PR8-induced IAV infection models was established in mice and cells to evaluate the protective effects of EC. EC treatment improved survival outcomes, markedly alleviated lung injury in a manner independent of direct viral inhibition, reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine expression, and improved mitochondrial function. Mechanistically, EC rescued the impaired autophagy flux induced by IAV infection, as evidenced by reduced p62 accumulation and enhanced mitochondrial clearance, and this effect required intact lysosomal degradation activity. Proteomic analysis further identified BNIP3L as a key regulator, and genetic knockdown of BNIP3L largely abolished EC-mediated protective phenotypes. EC significantly upregulated BNIP3L expression to promote mitochondrial clearance and maintain mitochondrial homeostasis. Metabolomic analysis showed that EC markedly reshaped host metabolic profiles associated with mitochondrial function in lung, with trigonelline identified as a key metabolite upon EC intervention. Functional experiments demonstrated that trigonelline recapitulated EC-like protective effects by facilitating autophagosome-lysosome fusion to restore BNIP3L-dependent mitochondrial clearance and attenuating inflammatory responses both in vitro and in vivo . Overall, EC alleviates IAV-induced lung injury by restoring BNIP3L-mediated mitochondrial clearance and mitochondrial homeostasis. Trigonelline serves as a functional metabolite and metabolic signature of this protective process, highlighting a potential link between plant-derived phenolic compounds, mitochondrial clearance regulation, and host metabolic reprogramming during viral infection.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the protective effects of ethyl caffeate (EC) against influenza A virus (IAV)-induced lung injury. It demonstrates that EC alleviates lung damage by restoring mitochondrial function and BNIP3L-dependent mitophagy. The research highlights the role of EC in reducing inflammation and improving mitochondrial homeostasis through autophagy flux and lysosomal degradation. Metabolomic analysis identifies trigonelline as a key metabolite involved in EC's protective mechanism. The findings suggest EC as a potential therapeutic agent for IAV-related lung injury, emphasizing the importance of mitochondrial quality control during viral infections. However, the study is limited to animal and cell models, and further research is needed to validate these results in humans.

abstract_zh: 甲型流感病毒(IAV)感染会引起严重的肺损伤,其特征是过度炎症和线粒体功能障碍,其中线粒体清除功能受损起着至关重要的作用。咖啡酸乙酯 (EC) 是一种源自膳食的生物活性酚类化合物,具有有效的抗炎和抗氧化特性。然而,其对 IAV 引发的肺损伤和线粒体质量控制功能障碍的保护作用仍不清楚。本研究在小鼠和细胞中建立了PR8诱导的IAV感染模型,以评估EC的保护作用。EC 治疗 改善了生存结果,以独立于直接病毒抑制的方式显着减轻了肺损伤,减少了促炎细胞因子的表达,并改善了线粒体功能。从机制上讲,EC 挽救了 IAV 感染引起的受损自噬流,p62 积累减少和线粒体清除增强证明了这一点,而这种作用需要完整的溶酶体降解活性。蛋白质组学分析进一步确定 BNIP3L 是一个关键的调节因子,并且 BNIP3L 的基因敲除很大程度上消除了 EC 介导的保护表型。EC 显着上调 BNIP3L 表达,促进线粒体清除并维持线粒体稳态。代谢组学分析表明,EC 显着重塑了与肺线粒体功能相关的 宿主 代谢谱,葫芦巴碱被确定为 EC 干预后的关键代谢物。功能实验表明,葫芦巴碱通过促进自噬体-溶酶体融合来恢复 BNIP3L 依赖性线粒体清除并减弱体外和体内炎症反应,从而重现 EC 样保护作用。总体而言,EC 通过恢复 BNIP3L 介导的线粒体清除和线粒体稳态来减轻 IAV 引起的肺损伤。葫芦巴碱作为这一保护过程的功能代谢物和代谢特征,突显了植物源性酚类化合物、线粒体清除调节和病毒感染期间 宿主 代谢重编程之间的潜在联系。

title: The Effect of Prevaccination Analgesics on Influenza Vaccine Immunogenicity and Effectiveness.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Analgesic medications are sometimes taken prior to vaccination to prevent local and systemic adverse reactions. Although studies have examined the association between postvaccination analgesic use and immunogenicity, few have evaluated the effects of prevaccination analgesic use. This analysis assessed antibody response, influenza-like illness (ILI), and influenza infection among adults with and without analgesic use before influenza vaccination. METHODS: The Pragmatic Assessment of Influenza Vaccine Effectiveness in the DoD (PAIVED) study was an open-label, randomized trial evaluating the effectiveness of FDA-licensed influenza vaccines during 4 influenza seasons in adult military healthcare beneficiaries. PAIVED participants with data on analgesic use within 24 hours before vaccination were included in this analysis if they either provided prevaccination and postvaccination venous blood samples or participated in weekly ILI surveillance. RESULTS: Among 684 PAIVED participants with prevaccination and postvaccination antibody titers, 10.4% (n = 71) reported analgesic use before influenza vaccination. Multivariable analyses showed no association between analgesic use and geometric mean titer fold change. There was a modest association between acetaminophen use and increased seroconversion to influenza A/H3N2 compared with no analgesic use (aIRR = 1.37; P = .022); however, this association was not significant in sensitivity analyses adjusting for multiple comparisons. Among 10 723 PAIVED participants with ILI surveillance data, 10.6% (n = 1140) reported prevaccination analgesic use. title: Three-Year Polymerase Chain Reaction-Based Surveillance of Respiratory Tract Infections in Adults and Seasonal Patterns.
abstract: Abstract Objective: This study investigated the aetiological composition, seasonal variation and risk factors of adult respiratory tract infections in Ganzhou, Jiangxi Province, during 2023–2025. Methods: A total of 8,493 adults (≥18 years) with respiratory symptoms were enrolled from a tertiary hospital during 2023–2025. Oropharyngeal and nasopharyngeal swabs were tested using multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) panels targeting six categories of seven respiratory pathogens: influenza A and B viruses, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), parainfluenza virus types I and III, adenovirus and Mycoplasma pneumoniae. Mixed infections (two or more pathogens) were reported separately. Data were analysed by univariate analysis and multivariate logistic regression. Results: The overall pathogen detection rate was 4.14% (352/8,493), comprising 325 single infections (92.33%) and 27 mixed infections (7.67%). Among single infections, M. pneumoniae (39.69%), influenza A virus (28.00%) and RSV (16.00%) predominated. Infections peaked in winter–spring (December–March). Age ≥65 years (OR = 2.35, 95% CI: 1.78–3.09), underlying diseases (OR = 2.41, 95% CI: 1.89–3.08) and emergency department admission (OR = 1.58, 95% CI: 1.24–2.01) were independent risk factors. Conclusion: Adult respiratory infections in Ganzhou show clear winter–spring seasonality, with M. pneumoniae, influenza A virus and RSV as leading pathogens. These findings support seasonally targeted surveillance – with enhanced monitoring for M. pneumoniae and influenza during winter–spring months – and prioritised vaccination, expanded diagnostic panels and early PCR-based diagnosis for adults aged ≥65 years and those with underlying diseases, thereby strengthening local respiratory infection prevention and control strategies.

title: Individual Preferences for Influenza Vaccine in Iran: A Discrete Choice Experiment.
abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aims Influenza vaccination is a key preventive measure against seasonal influenza. Understanding public preferences for influenza vaccine attributes is essential for designing effective vaccination strategies. This study examined individuals’ preferences for influenza vaccine attributes in Iran and identified factors associated with vaccine choice. Methods A discrete choice experiment (DCE) was conducted among 226 adults in Tehran province between September and December 2024. Seven vaccine attributes were evaluated: effectiveness, risk of severe side effects, risk of mild side effects, number of doses, duration of protection, location of manufacture, and price. Conditional and mixed logit models were used to estimate participants’ preferences, and model performance was assessed using the log‐likelihood, Akaike information criterion (AIC), and Bayesian information criterion (BIC). Results Vaccines with higher effectiveness were more likely to be selected, whereas higher risks of severe side effects and higher prices were associated with a lower likelihood of vaccine selection. The risk of mild side effects, duration of protection, and location of manufacture showed limited or no association with vaccine choice in the conditional logit model, although the mixed logit model suggested a lower preference for domestically manufactured vaccines. Preference heterogeneity was observed, with age, marital status, education, and health insurance status being associated with differences in preferences for specific vaccine attributes. Conclusion Vaccine effectiveness, safety, and affordability appeared to be the most important attributes associated with influenza vaccine choice in this study. These findings suggest that public health strategies emphasizing vaccine effectiveness and safety while improving affordability may help increase influenza vaccine uptake in Iran.

title: Climate-Driven Perturbations in Influenza Subtype Positivity Before and After the COVID-19 Pandemic: Observational Study.
abstract: Abstract Background The COVID-19 pandemic significantly altered global influenza transmission patterns. Whether the associations among meteorological conditions, visibility, and influenza subtype (A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and B/Victoria) positivity changed after the pandemic remains unclear. We compared these associations before and after the COVID-19 pandemic in northern China. Objective This study aimed to characterize changes in the associations of meteorological variables and visibility with influenza subtype positivity before and after the COVID-19 pandemic and to identify subtype-specific nonlinear patterns and thresholds. Methods Using 13 years of influenza surveillance and environmental data, we applied Extreme Gradient Boosting enhanced with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) to characterize the relative importance and direction of associations between environmental variables and influenza subtype positivity. Generalized additive models (GAMs) were subsequently used to characterize nonlinear association patterns and identify thresholds at which the direction of model-estimated associations changed. Results Absolute humidity (AH) remained the most influential environmental factor for A/H3N2 and A/H1N1, accounting for 32.2% and 38.5% of relative feature importance, respectively. Visibility increased in importance after the pandemic, rising from being the fourth to the second most influential environmental indicator. GAM analysis identified thresholds corresponding to points where the direction of the associations changed. For A/H3N2, AH below 4 g/m 3 was associated with positive SHAP values, whereas higher AH was predominantly associated with negative SHAP values. For A/H1N1, the direction of association changed at an AH threshold of 4.5 g/m 3 (95% CI 4.0-4.8) in the postpandemic period. Additionally, relative humidity (RH) demonstrated a complex nonlinear association with A/H3N2 positivity, with transition points at 45.1% (95% CI 43.5%-46.1%) and 69.7% (95% CI 69.2%-70.2%) in the prepandemic period and at 48.7% (95% CI 46.7%-50.4%) and 70.6% (95% CI 66.3%-72.6%) in the postpandemic period. RH values within these ranges were associated with negative SHAP values, whereas values outside these ranges were associated with positive SHAP values. In contrast, visibility showed opposing association patterns for the A/H3N2 and B/Victoria subtypes after the pandemic. Visibility below 17.1 km (95% CI 16.3-17.4) was associated with negative SHAP values for A/H3N2, whereas visibility below 18.4 km (95% CI 18.0-18.9) was associated with positive SHAP values for B/Victoria. Conclusions AH remained a key environmental determinant of influenza A subtype positivity, while visibility became more important after the pandemic and showed opposing association patterns for A/H3N2 and B/Victoria. The identified nonlinear thresholds highlight subtype-specific environmental associations and may inform influenza surveillance and risk assessment under changing environmental conditions.

analysis.study_design_and_population: This observational study compared associations of meteorological variables and visibility with influenza subtype positivity in northern China before and after the pandemic, using 13 years of influenza surveillance and environmental data.
analysis.methods: Extreme Gradient Boosting enhanced with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) was used to assess the relative importance and direction of associations between environmental variables and influenza subtype positivity. Generalized additive models (GAMs) were then applied to identify nonlinear patterns and thresholds.
analysis.main_results: Absolute humidity (AH) remained the most influential factor for A/H3N2 and A/H1N1, accounting for 32.2% and 38.5% of relative feature importance, respectively. For A/H1N1, the direction of association changed at an AH threshold of 4.5 g/m 3 (95% CI 4.0-4.8).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that absolute humidity (AH) remained a key environmental determinant of influenza A subtype positivity, while visibility became more important after the pandemic and showed opposing association patterns for A/H3N2 and B/Victoria. This study identified subtype-specific nonlinear thresholds, highlighting the importance of environmental factors in influenza dynamics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform influenza surveillance and risk assessment under changing environmental conditions, particularly in understanding how pandemic-related changes affect subtype-specific environmental associations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is observational and based on environmental and surveillance data, which may introduce biases and confounding factors. The evidence is strong as it uses advanced statistical methods and provides specific thresholds for environmental associations.

analysis.summary_en: This observational study investigated changes in the associations between meteorological conditions, visibility, and influenza subtype positivity before and after the COVID-19 pandemic in northern China. Using Extreme Gradient Boosting with SHAP and generalized additive models (GAMs), the researchers found that absolute humidity (AH) remained the most influential factor for A/H3N2 and A/H1N1, while visibility increased in importance post-pandemic. The study identified specific thresholds for AH and RH where the direction of associations changed, and noted opposing patterns for A/H3N2 and B/Victoria subtypes. These findings highlight the need for subtype-specific environmental monitoring in influenza surveillance and risk assessment, particularly under changing climatic conditions. The study's observational design and use of advanced statistical methods provide moderate confidence in its conclusions.

title_zh: COVID-19 大流行前后气候驱动的流感亚型阳性率扰动:观察研究。
source_body_en: Abstract Background The COVID-19 pandemic significantly altered global influenza transmission patterns. Whether the associations among meteorological conditions, visibility, and influenza subtype (A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and B/Victoria) positivity changed after the pandemic remains unclear. We compared these associations before and after the COVID-19 pandemic in northern China. Objective This study aimed to characterize changes in the associations of meteorological variables and visibility with influenza subtype positivity before and after the COVID-19 pandemic and to identify subtype-specific nonlinear patterns and thresholds. Methods Using 13 years of influenza surveillance and environmental data, we applied Extreme Gradient Boosting enhanced with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) to characterize the relative importance and direction of associations between environmental variables and influenza subtype positivity. Generalized additive models (GAMs) were subsequently used to characterize nonlinear association patterns and identify thresholds at which the direction of model-estimated associations changed. Results Absolute humidity (AH) remained the most influential environmental factor for A/H3N2 and A/H1N1, accounting for 32.2% and 38.5% of relative feature importance, respectively. Visibility increased in importance after the pandemic, rising from being the fourth to the second most influential environmental indicator. GAM analysis identified thresholds corresponding to points where the direction of the associations changed. For A/H3N2, AH below 4 g/m 3 was associated with positive SHAP values, whereas higher AH was predominantly associated with negative SHAP values. For A/H1N1, the direction of association changed at an AH threshold of 4.5 g/m 3 (95% CI 4.0-4.8) in the postpandemic period. Additionally, relative humidity (RH) demonstrated a complex nonlinear association with A/H3N2 positivity, with transition points at 45.1% (95% CI 43.5%-46.1%) and 69.7% (95% CI 69.2%-70.2%) in the prepandemic period and at 48.7% (95% CI 46.7%-50.4%) and 70.6% (95% CI 66.3%-72.6%) in the postpandemic period. RH values within these ranges were associated with negative SHAP values, whereas values outside these ranges were associated with positive SHAP values. In contrast, visibility showed opposing association patterns for the A/H3N2 and B/Victoria subtypes after the pandemic. Visibility below 17.1 km (95% CI 16.3-17.4) was associated with negative SHAP values for A/H3N2, whereas visibility below 18.4 km (95% CI 18.0-18.9) was associated with positive SHAP values for B/Victoria. Conclusions AH remained a key environmental determinant of influenza A subtype positivity, while visibility became more important after the pandemic and showed opposing association patterns for A/H3N2 and B/Victoria. The identified nonlinear thresholds highlight subtype-specific environmental associations and may inform influenza surveillance and risk assessment under changing environmental conditions.
abstract_zh: 摘要背景 COVID-19 大流行显着改变了全球流感 传播 模式。大流行后,气象条件、能见度和流感亚型(A/H1N1、A/H3N2 和 B/Victoria)阳性之间的关联是否发生变化仍不清楚。我们比较了中国北方 COVID-19 大流行前后的这些关联。目的 本研究旨在描述 COVID-19 大流行前后气象变量和能见度与流感亚型阳性之间关联的变化,并确定亚型特异性的非线性模式和阈值。方法 使用 13 年的流感 监测 和环境数据,我们应用沙普利附加解释 (SHAP) 增强的极限梯度增强来表征环境变量与流感亚型阳性之间关联的相对重要性和方向。随后使用广义加性模型(GAM)来表征非线性关联模式并识别模型估计关联方向发生变化的阈值。结果绝对湿度(AH)仍然是对 A/H3N2 和 A/H1N1 影响最大的环境因素,分别占相对特征重要性的 32.2% 和 38.5%。疫情爆发后,能见度变得更加重要,从第四位上升到第二位最具影响力的环境指标。GAM 分析确定了与关联方向发生变化的点相对应的阈值。对于A/H3N2,低于4 g/m 3 的AH 与正SHAP 值相关,而较高的AH 主要与负SHAP 值相关。对于 A/H1N1,在大流行后时期,关联方向在 AH 阈值 4.5 g/m 3 (95% CI 4.0-4.8) 处发生变化。此外,相对湿度 (RH) 与 A/H3N2 阳性呈复杂的非线性关联,大流行前的转变点分别为 45.1% (95% CI 43.5%-46.1%) 和 69.7% (95% CI 69.2%-70.2%),以及 48.7% (95% CI 46.7%-50.4%) 和 70.6% (95% CI 66.3%-72.6%)在大流行后时期。这些范围内的 RH 值与负 SHAP 值相关,而这些范围之外的值与正 SHAP 值相关。相比之下,大流行后 A/H3N2 和 B/Victoria 亚型的可见性显示出相反的关联模式。能见度低于 17.1 公里 (95% CI 16.3-17.4) 与 A/H3N2 的负 SHAP 值相关,而能见度低于 18.4 公里 (95% CI 18.0-18.9) 与 B/Victoria 的正 SHAP 值相关。结论 AH 仍然是甲型流感亚型阳性的关键环境决定因素,而大流行后可见性变得更加重要,并且显示出 A/H3N2 和 B/Victoria 的相反关联模式。确定的非线性阈值突出了亚型特定的环境关联,并可能为流感 监测 和不断变化的环境条件下的风险评估提供信息。

title: Epidemiologic Variability and Clinical Severity Across 11 Influenza Seasons in Children.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Influenza is a major cause of respiratory illness, contributing substantially to morbidity and mortality in children. Seasonal influenza epidemics were profoundly disrupted by the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. Whether the clinical presentation and disease severity differ according to influenza virus type and subtype remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to describe temporal changes in epidemiology, clinical characteristics, outcomes and healthcare utilization among laboratory-confirmed pediatric influenza cases over 11 seasons and to explore associations between virus type/subtype and clinically important outcomes. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study at a tertiary pediatric hospital, including all laboratory-confirmed influenza cases identified in children presenting with acute respiratory infection between July 2015 and June 2026, and analyzed the distribution of cases and their demographic and clinical characteristics. RESULTS: Influenza was detected in 3105 children (median age, 4 years), the majority of whom were previously healthy (82.4%). Within this cohort, hospitalization was required in 17.9% of cases, with 1.1% requiring intensive care admission, and 22.8% developing complications, including encephalitis and sepsis. Influenza circulation patterns, including the timing of peak activity and the duration of annual epidemics, varied over time. After an 18-month absence of reported cases during the COVID-19 pandemic, the 2021-2022 season was marked by a substantial resurgence, followed by 2 years of atypical year-round circulation before returning to the usual seasonal pattern. Influenza A accounted for 72.3% of cases, with alternating predominance of virus types and subtypes without a consistent epidemiologic pattern. In a restricted type/subtype analysis, influenza A(H1N1) cases had a higher frequency of hospitalization and recorded moderate-to-severe complications, and this association remained statistically significant after multivariable analysis. CONCLUSIONS: Influenza was associated with clinically important illness and healthcare use among children in this hospital-based cohort, most commonly among otherwise healthy children, highlighting the importance of influenza prevention strategies. During and after the COVID-19 pandemic, influenza epidemiology changed markedly, underscoring the need for continued surveillance.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the epidemiologic variability and clinical severity of influenza across 11 seasons in children, focusing on seasonal influenza viruses. It highlights the changing patterns of influenza circulation, particularly during and after the COVID-19 pandemic, and the association between influenza A(H1N1) and higher hospitalization rates and complications. The study is based on a retrospective observational design at a tertiary pediatric hospital, analyzing laboratory-confirmed cases from 2015 to 2026. The results show that influenza A accounted for the majority of cases, with varying predominance of subtypes. The findings emphasize the need for ongoing surveillance and prevention strategies, especially for otherwise healthy children who are most affected. The evidence is strong, with a high confidence rating, but the study design is limited to a single hospital setting, which may affect generalizability.

title_zh: 儿童 11 个流感季节的流行病学变异和临床严重程度。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Influenza is a major cause of respiratory illness, contributing substantially to morbidity and mortality in children. Seasonal influenza epidemics were profoundly disrupted by the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. Whether the clinical presentation and disease severity differ according to influenza virus type and subtype remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to describe temporal changes in epidemiology, clinical characteristics, outcomes and healthcare utilization among laboratory-confirmed pediatric influenza cases over 11 seasons and to explore associations between virus type/subtype and clinically important outcomes. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study at a tertiary pediatric hospital, including all laboratory-confirmed influenza cases identified in children presenting with acute respiratory infection between July 2015 and June 2026, and analyzed the distribution of cases and their demographic and clinical characteristics. RESULTS: Influenza was detected in 3105 children (median age, 4 years), the majority of whom were previously healthy (82.4%). Within this cohort, hospitalization was required in 17.9% of cases, with 1.1% requiring intensive care admission, and 22.8% developing complications, including encephalitis and sepsis. Influenza circulation patterns, including the timing of peak activity and the duration of annual epidemics, varied over time. After an 18-month absence of reported cases during the COVID-19 pandemic, the 2021-2022 season was marked by a substantial resurgence, followed by 2 years of atypical year-round circulation before returning to the usual seasonal pattern. Influenza A accounted for 72.3% of cases, with alternating predominance of virus types and subtypes without a consistent epidemiologic pattern. In a restricted type/subtype analysis, influenza A(H1N1) cases had a higher frequency of hospitalization and recorded moderate-to-severe complications, and this association remained statistically significant after multivariable analysis. CONCLUSIONS: Influenza was associated with clinically important illness and healthcare use among children in this hospital-based cohort, most commonly among otherwise healthy children, highlighting the importance of influenza prevention strategies. During and after the COVID-19 pandemic, influenza epidemiology changed markedly, underscoring the need for continued surveillance.
abstract_zh: 背景:流感是呼吸系统疾病的主要原因,极大地增加了儿童的发病率和 死亡率。季节性流感 流行病受到 2019 年冠状病毒病 (COVID-19) 大流行的严重破坏。临床表现和疾病严重程度是否因流感病毒类型和亚型而异仍不完全清楚。本研究旨在描述 11 个季节内实验室确诊的儿科流感病例中 流行病学、临床特征、结果和医疗保健利用的时间变化,并探讨病毒类型/亚型与临床重要结果之间的关联。方法:我们对某三级儿科医院2015年7月至2026年6月期间所有实验室确诊的急性呼吸道感染儿童流感病例进行回顾性观察研究,分析病例分布及其人口学和临床特征。结果:3105 名儿童(中位年龄为 4 岁)中检测出流感,其中大多数先前健康(82.4%)。在该 队列研究 中,17.9% 的病例需要住院治疗,其中 1.1% 需要入院重症监护,22.8% 出现并发症,包括脑炎和败血症。流感的传播模式,包括高峰活动的时间和年度流行病的持续时间,随着时间的推移而变化。在 COVID-19 大流行期间连续 18 个月没有报告病例后,2021-2022 年季节出现了大幅复苏,随后经历了 2 年的非典型全年循环,然后又恢复到通常的季节模式。甲型流感占病例的 72.3%,病毒类型和亚型交替为主,没有一致的流行病学模式。在限制型/亚型分析中,甲型H1N1流感病例的住院频率较高,并有中重度并发症,且在多变量分析后这种关联仍具有统计学显着性。结论:流感与 队列研究 医院儿童的临床重要疾病和医疗保健使用相关,最常见于其他健康儿童,这凸显了流感预防策略的重要性。在 COVID-19 大流行期间和之后,流感 流行病学 发生了显着变化,强调了继续使用 监测 的必要性。

title: Influenza Vaccination and Disease Severity Among Older Adults Hospitalized with Influenza in France: A Nationwide Cohort Study, 2016-2024
abstract: Objective: Seasonal influenza remains a major cause of severe morbidity and mortality among older adults, despite vaccine availability. We assessed whether influenza vaccination was associated with reduced disease severity among adults aged 65 years or more hospitalized with influenza in France. Methods and Analysis We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using the French National Health Data System (SNDS). Adults aged 65 years or more hospitalized with confirmed influenza (ICD-10 codes: J09 or J10) between October 2016 and December 2024 were included, excluding 2020-2021. Vaccination status was identified from reimbursed community pharmacy dispensing records. Entropy balancing was used to balance sociodemographic characteristics, chronic conditions pneumococcal vaccination, and COVID-19 vaccination. Weighted regression models estimated adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) for invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), intensive care unit (ICU) admission, in-hospital death, and a composite severe outcome. Multistate survival models assessed transitions specific hazard ratios (HR) between hospitalization, ICU, discharge, and in-hospital death. Results Among 132,443 influenza-associated hospitalizations, 72,852 (55%) occurred among vaccinated patients and 59,591 (45%) among unvaccinated patients. Vaccinated patients were older (mean age, 82.3 vs 79.3 years). IMV occurred in 2128 vaccinated (2.9%) and 2544 unvaccinated (4.3%) hospitalizations (aRR, 0.88; 95%CI: 0.83 to 0.93). In-hospital death occurred in 6300 (8.6%) and 4952 (8.3%), respectively (aRR, 0.90; 95%CI: 0.87 to 0.93). Vaccination was also associated with a lower risk of the composite outcome (aRR, 0.96; 95%CI: 0.94 to 0.98), but not ICU admission (aRR, 0.99; 95%CI: 0.96 to 1.01). Among patients admitted to ICU, vaccination was associated with a lower hazard of death (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.85; 95%CI: 0.78 to 0.92) and a 2-day reduction in the median time to discharge. Conclusion In this nationwide cohort study, influenza vaccination was associated with lower risks of IMV and in-hospital death among older adults hospitalized with influenza. These findings are consistent with possible attenuation of disease severity and support efforts to improve influenza vaccination among older adults.

title: Reconstructing substitution histories on phylogenies, with accuracy, precision, and coverage.
abstract: Ancestral sequences and substitution histories are usually averaged out in phylogenetic inference and are therefore not reported to the user. However, they can be recovered through ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR) and stochastic character mapping. By implementing and validating a new ASR and stochastic mapping package compatible with both single-locus and multispecies coalescent analysis, we show how reconstructing substitution histories can enhance the information gained about the tempo and mode of molecular evolution. We observe that known substitution histories (simulated and empirical) are recovered more accurately and precisely on time trees compared with unconstrained and non-ultrametric substitution trees that lack temporal directionality (maximum likelihood and Bayesian). We show that codon-partition models with site-rate heterogeneity, based on the four nucleotide characters, can effectively approximate the histories of synonymous and non-synonymous change, while requiring far less runtime than computationally demanding codon models that require 61 characters. In turn, this provides low-bias estimation of dN/dS that is robust to non-stationarity in GC content, codon usage bias, and nucleotide exchangeability rates. Lastly, using three case studies, we demonstrate how the approach can recover expected patterns in molecular evolution and pathogen transmission: that i) smaller-bodied mammalian species tend to have faster synonymous substitution rates than larger relatives, ii) amino acid substitutions are correlated with 3Di structural changes in aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, and iii) influenza A virus spread more frequently to nearby locations than distant ones, in a major H3N2 outbreak in New Zealand. These three trends were more pronounced when based on count estimates derived from stochastic mapping, relative to parametric rates and distances. Our open-source code comes with a user-friendly graphical interface, as the BeastMap package for BEAST 2; supporting a wide range of clock, site, and tree models and data types - including insertions and deletions - within a Bayesian phylogenetic framework.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limitations of phylogenetic inference by improving the accuracy and precision of reconstructing substitution histories, which are typically averaged out and not reported to users.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study implemented and validated a new ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR) and stochastic mapping package, demonstrating its application through three case studies involving seasonal influenza viruses.
analysis.methods: The methods involved developing a package compatible with both single-locus and multispecies coalescent analysis, using a Bayesian phylogenetic framework to support various clock, site, and tree models, including insertions and deletions.
analysis.main_results: Known substitution histories, both simulated and empirical, were recovered more accurately and precisely on time trees compared to unconstrained and non-ultrametric substitution trees.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that their approach provides a more reliable estimation of dN/dS, which is robust to non-stationarity in GC content, codon usage bias, and nucleotide exchangeability rates.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the understanding of molecular evolution patterns in seasonal influenza viruses, particularly in relation to transmission dynamics and structural changes in viral proteins.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges that codon-partition models with site-rate heterogeneity based on four nucleotide characters can approximate substitution histories more efficiently than computationally demanding models, though the evidence is based on simulated and empirical data.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a new ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR) and stochastic mapping package designed to improve the accuracy and precision of reconstructing substitution histories in phylogenetic analysis. The approach is validated through simulated and empirical data, demonstrating its effectiveness in capturing molecular evolution patterns. The study highlights that time trees provide better recovery of substitution histories compared to non-ultrametric trees. It also shows that the method can approximate synonymous and non-synonymous changes with less computational demand. The findings have implications for understanding molecular evolution and transmission dynamics in seasonal influenza viruses, particularly in relation to structural changes in aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases and geographic spread patterns. The study's results are based on three case studies, and the method is implemented as an open-source package with a user-friendly interface. However, the study notes that the approach may not fully capture all complexities of molecular evolution without further validation.

abstract_zh: 祖先序列和替代历史通常在系统发育推断中进行平均,因此不会报告给用户。然而,它们可以通过祖先序列重建(ASR)和随机字符映射来恢复。通过实施和验证与单位点和多物种聚结分析兼容的新 ASR 和随机作图包,我们展示了重建取代历史如何增强获得的有关分子 进化 的节奏和模式的信息。我们观察到,与缺乏时间方向性(最大似然和贝叶斯)的无约束和非超度量替代树相比,已知的替代历史(模拟和经验)在时间树上恢复得更准确和精确。我们表明,基于四个核苷酸字符的具有位点速率异质性的密码子划分模型可以有效地近似同义和非同义变化的历史,同时比需要 61 个字符的计算要求高的密码子模型所需的运行时间要少得多。反过来,这提供了 dN/dS 的低偏差估计,对 GC 含量、密码子使用偏差和核苷酸交换率的非平稳性具有鲁棒性。最后,通过三个案例研究,我们证明了该方法如何恢复分子 进化 和病原体 传播 的预期模式:i) 体型较小的哺乳动物物种往往比体型较大的亲属具有更快的同义替换率,ii) 氨基酸替换与氨酰基-tRNA 合成酶中的 3Di 结构变化相关,以及 iii) 在主要的 H3N2 病毒中,甲型流感病毒传播到附近的位置比远处的位置更频繁新西兰的 暴发。当基于随机映射得出的计数估计(相对于参数率和距离)时,这三种趋势更加明显。我们的开源代码带有用户友好的图形界面,如BEAST 2的BeastMap包;在贝叶斯系统发育框架内支持各种时钟、位点和树模型和数据类型(包括插入和删除)。

title: Outcomes of elderly hospitalized patients with influenza after the COVID-19 pandemic: decline of functional independence and frailty.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Influenza remains a heavy burden to the elderly and the situation has been affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. The objective of this study was to clarify outcomes of elderly hospitalized patients with influenza after the COVID-19 pandemic. METHODS: The clinical data of patients 65 years of age or older who were severely ill with influenza and required hospitalization in one center were gathered between September 2023 and March 2026 (3 influenza seasons after the COVID-19 pandemic). The outcomes, functional independence, and frailty of them were analyzed. RESULTS: A total of 210 elderly patients were enrolled. The median age was 79 and 32 cases were judged as having mild or more frailty by the clinical frailty scale (CFS) before admission. Pneumonia was the most common disease indicated as cause for hospitalization, followed by a poor general condition and heart failure. The median duration of hospitalization was 13 days and in-hospital deaths were recorded for 17 patients (8.1%). Sixty cases changed hospital due to further treatment or deterioration of activity of daily living, and the functional independence measure (FIM) of 37 cases (17.6%) remained under a score of 70 even after rehabilitation. The CFSs worsened in 19 cases (9.0%) at the time of discharge. CONCLUSIONS: Influenza infection remains a heavy burden among the elderly after the COVID-19 pandemic. The elderly tend to lose functional independence and fail to frailty even after recovery from acute illness. Preventive measures for influenza to avoid admission, including vaccination, will be essential. (Influenza Internet Survey, UMIN000015989).

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the outcomes of elderly hospitalized patients with influenza after the COVID-19 pandemic. It highlights that influenza remains a significant burden for the elderly, with functional independence and frailty being major concerns even after recovery. The study found that 8.1% of patients experienced in-hospital deaths, and 17.6% had functional independence scores below 70 post-rehabilitation. The authors emphasize the importance of preventive measures, such as vaccination, to reduce the risk of hospitalization. The evidence is based on data collected from one center over three influenza seasons post-pandemic, and the findings suggest a continued need for targeted interventions in this vulnerable population. However, the study does not provide information on its limitations, which may affect the confidence in its conclusions.

abstract_zh: 背景:流感仍然是老年人的沉重负担,并且情况受到了 COVID-19 大流行的影响。本研究的目的是澄清 COVID-19 大流行后患有流感的老年住院患者的结局。方法:收集 2023 年 9 月至 2026 年 3 月(COVID-19 大流行后的 3 个流感季节)期间,65 岁或以上患有严重流感并需要在一个中心住院的患者的临床数据。对它们的结果、功能独立性和脆弱性进行了分析。结果:共有210名老年患者入组。中位年龄79岁,入院前根据临床衰弱量表(CFS)判断为轻度以上衰弱者32例。肺炎是导致住院的最常见疾病,其次是全身状况不佳和心力衰竭。中位住院时间为 13 天,17 名患者 (8.1%) 发生院内死亡。60例因进一步治疗或日常生活能力恶化而转院,37例(17.6%)的功能独立测量(FIM)即使在康复后仍低于70分。19 例(9.0%)出院时 CFS 恶化。结论:在 COVID-19 大流行之后,流感感染仍然是老年人的沉重负担。老年人往往会失去功能独立性,即使在急性疾病康复后也不会变得虚弱。避免入院的流感预防措施(包括 疫苗接种)至关重要。(流感互联网调查,UMIN000015989)。

title: Comparison of Dissemination of Aerosol and Splatter during Ultrasonic Scaling using Different Masks: A Pilot Study with Relevance to Respiratory Infection Transmission
abstract: Abstract Background: Dentists are routinely exposed to a high amount of micro-organism load due to primarily being responsible for the treatment of the structures if the mouth – which is a well-known source of huge bacterial loads. Also, as COVID-19 recently affected the entire world, masks thus were considered to act as a comprehensive strategy of measures to suppress transmission. However, the relevance of aerosol and respiratory infection control extends beyond COVID-19, as respiratory pathogens including seasonal influenza viruses such as influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, commonly referred to as swine flu, influenza A(H3N2), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and other respiratory viruses continue to circulate and may be transmitted through respiratory particles. Aim: To compare the dissemination of aerosol and splatter during ultrasonic scaling using different masks. Method: In this study we evaluated the dissemination of four masks that is N-95 with respirator, N-95 without respirator, a combination of cloth mask and N-95 without respirator, and normal surgical mask by calculating the surface are of filter paper with the help of a previously marked scale which was divided into one-centimeter squares. Results: Best protection was seen to be offered by the combined use of the double masking – N-95 without filter plus cloth mask, followed by N-95 mask alone and then the surgical mask.
