analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess whether prior infection with A(H1N1)pdm09 virus provides cross-protection against H5N1 and H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses, which have raised public health concerns due to their spread among birds and mammals.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a preimmune ferret model, with 12 ferrets serologically naive to seasonal influenza viruses, and challenged them with H5N1 and H5N5 viruses. Three ferrets per group were euthanized on day 4 postinfection to assess viral dissemination.
analysis.methods: The researchers infected ferrets with A(H1N1)pdm09 virus and confirmed seroconversion using a hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) assay. They then challenged these preimmune ferrets with H5N1 and H5N5 viruses and monitored clinical signs, weight loss, and viral shedding.
analysis.main_results: Results showed that prior A(H1N1)pdm09 immunity conferred partial protection against both H5N1 and H5N5 viruses, with slightly reduced protection against H5N5, potentially due to the absence of cross-reactive N5 neuraminidase antibodies.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that immunity from A(H1N1)pdm09 infection may offer some cross-protection against H5N1 and H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses, highlighting the potential role of HA stalk antibodies in this cross-reactivity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results have implications for understanding cross-protection against emerging H5N1 and H5N5 viruses, which could inform surveillance and vaccine development strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a ferret model and does not account for human immune responses, but the evidence is strong due to the controlled experimental design and clear results.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether prior infection with A(H1N1)pdm09 virus provides cross-protection against H5N1 and H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses. Ferrets infected with A(H1N1)pdm09 were challenged with H5N1 and H5N5 viruses, and results showed partial protection against both, with slightly less protection against H5N5. The findings suggest that HA stalk antibodies may mediate cross-protection, which has implications for understanding immune responses to emerging H5 viruses. The study's use of a controlled ferret model provides strong evidence, though limitations include the absence of human data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估先前感染 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 病毒是否可以提供针对 H5N1 和 H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b 病毒的交叉保护,这些病毒由于在鸟类和哺乳动物中传播而引起了公共卫生问题。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用了免疫前雪貂模型,其中 12 只雪貂在血清学上对 季节性流感 病毒不敏感,并用 H5N1 和 H5N5 病毒对它们进行攻击。每组三只雪貂在感染后第 4 天被安乐死,以评估病毒传播情况。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员用 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 病毒感染雪貂,并使用血凝抑制 (HAI) 测定证实了血清转化。然后,他们用 H5N1 和 H5N5 病毒攻击这些未免疫的雪貂,并监测临床症状、体重减轻和病毒脱落。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果显示,先前的 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 免疫可对 H5N1 和 H5N5 病毒提供部分保护,但对 H5N5 病毒的保护略有减弱,这可能是由于缺乏交叉反应性 N5 神经氨酸酶抗体。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 感染的免疫力可能对 H5N1 和 H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b 病毒提供一些交叉保护,突出了 HA 茎抗体在这种交叉反应中的潜在作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果对于了解针对新出现的 H5N1 和 H5N5 病毒的交叉保护具有重要意义,这可以为 监测 和 疫苗 的开发策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于雪貂模型,并未考虑人类 免疫应答,但由于受控的实验设计和明确的结果,证据是强有力的。

media_mentions.content: Avian Flu Diary Covering Pandemic and Seasonal Flu, Emerging Infectious Diseases, public health, community & Individual preparedness. NOTE: All AFD blogs are written by a human - any mistakes are solely mine. Monday, November 16, 2026 South Korea APQA Issues HPAI Alert #19,418 While H5N1 remains the primary global HPAI threat, since 2022 we've watched a divergent subtype - H5N5 - establish itself and persist in high latitude regions of the Northern Hemisphere, and last year we followed the first incursion of an H5N9 subtype into South Korea (see South Korea: H5N9 Rising). South Korea's MAFRA reported 62 outbreaks in poultry over the 2025-2026 avian flu season, and of those, 57 were H5N1 while only 5 (8%) were H5N9. Nine days ago, in South Korea: MAFRA Reports 2 Outbreaks of HPAI H5N9 in Poultry & Ducks, we looked at early season reports indicating 2 of the first 3 poultry outbreaks this fall were H5N9. Since then 3 more poultry farm outbreaks have been reported (Ganghwa, Jincheon, Paju ), which MAFRA has described as a `mix' of H5N9 and H5N1. Yesterday, MAFRA reported a non-farm `ornamental bird' operation was positive for HPAI H5, with NA typing pending. Today, local media is reporting it to be H5N9, but again, I haven't found official confirmation. This year South Korean avian flu reports (which are already hampered by machine translation) seem less detailed. Below, you'll find their Risk Alert lists 6 poultry outbreaks, and 10 wild bird detections, but doesn't provide a breakdown by subtype. It would appear that somewhere between 3 and 5 of the first 7 outbreaks in South Korea this fall are due to H5N9. Even assuming the lowest number, that would represent a significant shift from the 8% reported last year. First the AQPA statement, after which I'll have a bit more. Animal Quarantine Agency Issues Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (AI) Risk Alert Department in charge Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency Author Lee Hyun-jik 82 2026-11-14 The Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency ( Acting Director Jeong Seung-gyo , hereinafter the Agency ) issued a “ Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (AI ) Risk Advisory ” on November 13 as the risk of highly pathogenic avian influenza (AI ) outbreaks in domestic poultry farms increased , and simultaneously disseminated the quarantine measures to poultry farms , livestock facilities , and vehicle drivers nationwide through text messages , notifications , etc. Measures to raise awareness among livestock stakeholders and strengthen disease control measures in accordance with the Avian Influenza Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) when warning signs, such as the detection of multiple AI antigens in wild birds, occur. Since highly pathogenic avian influenza (AI) antigens were detected in wild bird droppings collected at Suncheon Bay in Gwangju, Jeollanam-do (October 12 ), a total of 10 cases of highly pathogenic avian influenza (AI) have been detected to date. In poultry farms as well, following the outbreak at a laying hen farm in Yeoncheon, Gyeonggi-do (November 3), a total of 6 cases of highly pathogenic avian influenza (AI) have occurred at a broiler duck farm in Jangheung, Gwangju, Jeollanam-do (November 5 ) , a laying hen farm in Yeoju , Gyeonggi -do (November 6 ), a laying hen farm in Ganghwa, Incheon (November 11), a breeding duck farm in Jincheon, Chungcheongbuk-do (November 12), and a quail farm in Paju, Gyeonggi-do ( November 12 ) . In particular , during this winter season, two serotypes, H5N1 and H5N9 , have been identified and are occurring frequently in a short period , making thorough disease control management necessary . * ( Wild Birds ) 10 cases ( Suncheon Suncheon Bay 1, Gimpo Lower Han River 2, Yongin Cheongmicheon 1, Hongcheon Yangdeokwoncheon 2, Jeonnam Gwangju Gwangsan-gu Hwangnyonggang 1, Yeoju Namhangang 1, Nonsan Yeonsancheon 1, Jeongeup Dongjingang 1) * ( Poultry Farms ) 6 cases ( Yeoncheon Laying Hen 1, Jangheung Broiler Duck 1, Yeoju Laying Hen 1, Ganghwa Laying Hen 1, Jincheon Breeding Duck 1, Paju Quail 1) In addition , monitoring of the movement of migratory birds equipped with GPS trackers revealed that the southward migration of birds appears to be in full swing, as evidenced by the confirmation that mallards residing in Baiqing, Jilin Province, China, migrated south to Korea on November 6 and were inhabiting Uljin, North Gyeongsang Province , on November 7. In particular , the risk is increasing, as highly pathogenic AI was detected in Mandarin ducks captured in the Hwangryong River in Gwangju , South Jeolla Province, and Eurasian wigeon captured in Yeonsan Stream in Nonsan, South Chungcheong Province . Meanwhile , in Japan , after highly pathogenic AI antigens were detected in wild birds and the environment ( water ) in Akita, Hokkaido , and Kagoshima prefectures on November 2 , suspected cases of highly pathogenic AI were reported at a laying hen farm in Kyoto Prefecture (200,000 birds ) and laying hens in Chiba Prefecture (40,000 birds ) . * Japan Outbreak Status : 3 cases of wild birds ( including environment ) ( 2 H5N1 , 1 H5 ) , 2 cases reported from poultry farms Given the current status of wild bird arrivals in Korea, antigen detection, and outbreaks in neighboring countries , there is a very high risk of transmission of highly pathogenic avian influenza (AI) virus from wild birds to poultry farms this winter . Accordingly , the Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency has issued a “ Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (AI) Risk Advisory ” to raise awareness among livestock industry stakeholders and strengthen disease control measures . It has urged poultry farms to comply with disease control rules , including: △ two- stage disinfection of vehicles entering the farm ; △ wearing protective clothing and dedicated shoes and thorough personal disinfection for those entering the farm ; △ closing secondary entrances and back doors of barns without anterooms ; and △ changing into dedicated boots and disinfecting hands in the anteroom when entering the barn. At the same time , the agency plans to further strengthen inspections through the central inspection team of the Animal Disease Control Center regarding whether livestock vehicles are entering farms and whether disinfection is being carried out at designated disinfection facilities . Jeong Seung-kyo, Acting Head of the Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency, stated , “ With the recent increase in farm outbreaks and the expected arrival of migratory birds starting in November , we are in a grave situation where outbreaks could occur anywhere in the country, ” and urged poultry farmers to “ thoroughly implement farm-level quarantine measures, taking into account that virus contamination levels around farms and outside livestock barns are also rising significantly . ” In early 2014, an upstart H5N8 subtype abruptly appeared in South Korea, rapidly decimated their poultry industry, and then spread globally via migratory birds. Over the next 6 years it became the dominant global HPAI subtype, and sparked massive epizootics in Europe, the United States, and the Middle East. Its saving grace was that - unlike older H5N1 strains - it appeared less likely to infect humans. It wasn't until 2021 that the first human infections were reported (see Russian Media Reports 7 Human Infections With Avian H5N8), and by then H5N1 was on the upswing. While the significance or ultimate impact of this apparent rise in H5N9 is far from clear, it does remind us that HPAI is constantly changing. And that what first appears in South Korea, doesn't always stay in South Korea. Sunday, November 15, 2026 Canada: CFIA Statement on H5N1 Outbreak At Saskatchewan Poultry Show Posted on Saskatchewan Poultry Association Group Facebook page #19,417 Yesterday, CBC News reported Avian flu outbreak at national poultry show spreads to other provinces: CFIA, citing receipt of a CFIA statement. I was unable to find it on the CFIA website, but did locate a copy on the Saskatchewan Poultry Association Group Facebook page (above). The text reads: Canadian Food Inspection Agency November 13, 2026 Important Notice: Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) Exposure In Canada, Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) is a federally reportable disease under the Health of Animals Act for all animals, meaning any suspected or confirmed case must be reported immediately to the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA). The CFIA has detected a case of highly pathogenic avian influenza associated with a poultry show held on November 07, 2026 by the American Poultry Association for District 11 in Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan. If you showed birds at the event, or purchased or sold birds at the event, please immediately contact the CFIA's sick bird call line at 1-403-338-5225 if the CFIA has not already contacted you. If you attended the event without showing, purchasing, or selling birds, but you have birds of your own at home, please monitor them for any signs of illness. The incubation period of HPAL ranges from 2 to 14 days and it can be transmitted to other birds in multiple ways, such as birds having direct or indirect contact with infected birds, or through the movement of contaminated clothing/footwear to other groups of birds. If your own birds display any clinical signs which could be associated with highly pathogenic avian influenza (ex. lethargic, not eating, swollen cyes/wattles/combs, respiratory signs, unexpected decrease in egg production, or deaths), immediately contact the CFIA's sick bird call line at 1-403-338-5225 to report this suspicion of Thank you for your cooperation in helping to control this outbreak. For more information regarding highly pathogenic avian influenza, visit: https://inspection.canada.ca/en/animal-health/terrestrial-animals/diseases/reportable/avian-influenza CFIA reported their first outbreak in poultry of the fall on September 10th, followed by a slow ramping up of cases through the rest of September (n=8) and October (n=13). Over the past 5 days, however, the number of outbreaks has risen sharply (n=11). Poultry exhibitions tend to be held in the fall, since adult birds molt in the summer and typically regain peak appearance in October and November, chicks hatched in the spring reach full adult size by autumn, and transport of birds is easier during cooler weather (less heat stress). Unfortunately, this also corresponds with the fall bird migration and increased risk of HPAI. While this Saskatchewan event appears to be one of the last big events this year in Canada, the American Poultry Association still lists a number of large events scheduled over the next two months. HPAI outbreaks traced to poultry exhibitions in North America have been rare thus far due to biosecurity measures in place and a willingness to cancel events, but we have seen numerous outbreaks linked to live bird markets (see USDA Reports Another H5N1 Outbreak at a Live Bird Market (Pennsylvania)). Each year it seems to get a little bit harder to prevent and/or contain HPAI. While fortuitous evolution might someday attenuate those risks, so far, we've seen little sign of that happening. Saturday, November 14, 2026 For When The Bough Breaks CDC Infographic #19,416 Over the past 20 years the secondary focus of this blog has been on personal preparedness, and the growing fragility our our increasingly high-tech dependent infrastructure. Much of this comes from my 15 years of living aboard boats, and constantly thinking about what could fail (usually at the worst possible moment), and how to limit its impact. The events of the past few days (Microsoft outage, FAA 4-hour emergency groundstop, and several very large cyber-heists) remind us how fragile or vulnerable our systems are. Last January, in NERC: Long-Term Reliability Assessment (Jan 2026), we looked (again) at growing concerns over the stability of the nation's electrical grid, followed last May by NERC Issues Level 3 Alert As Grid Faces `Unprecedented Challenges' Due to Surge In Large Power Consumers. Every four years the ASCE (American Society of Civil Engineers) releases a report card on America’s infrastructure, and their most recent report (2025) warns that our cumulative GPA for infrastructure sits at only a C, and one of our most vulnerable infrastructures is the electrical grid (D+). This D+ rating is shared by Aviation, Dams, Roads, Levees, Wastewater, and Schools, while Stormwater and Transit are rated even lower. And every day that passes without addressing these problems only increases the risks. Regardless of what conspires to bring these systems down (age, neglect, deliberate sabotage, etc.), the impact will often first fall upon the American public. I was in New Orleans 5 weeks after Hurricane Katrina in 2005, and there was still no electricity, or running water, across most of the city. The streets were lined with debris and dead refrigerators filled with rotting food, pharmacies were still boarded up, and any semblance of normalcy was still months away. In 2014's Water, Water, Everywhere But Not A Drop To Drink we saw hundreds of thousands of Ohio residents without potable water for days due to harmful toxins produced by a microcystis algae bloom. This was neither the first or last such event. A similar emergency was declared in Oregon in 2018 (see Tapping Into Your Preps). (2018 advisory) Eight years ago, in NIAC: Surviving A Catastrophic Power Outage, we looked at a presidential commission's report on the risks of a major, prolonged, grid collapse. https://www.hsdl.org/?view&did=819354 This 92-page report was released a little more than a year after hurricane ravaged Puerto Rico suffered the longest (11-month) grid failure in American History and a year following another report - DHS: NIAC Cyber Threat Report - August 2017 - that warned of growing cyber threats to our critical infrastructure and called for `bold, decisive actions'. Over the past 10 years I've gone through 2 hurricane-induced extended (4-7 day) power outages, and one prolonged community well failure, that had me relying on my personal preps for food, water, and power for days. Yet I've been lucky. Many others have had to deal with far worse. In recent months we've seen increased calls by governments around the world for increased personal preparedness (see UK National Risk Register 2026 - Urges Citizen Preparedness). While the reasons given are often vague, concerns over natural or man-made disasters appear to be rising. California and the Pacific Northwest are bracing for what could be an unprecedented winter El Nino (see California Declares State of Emergency to Bolster Statewide El Niño Preparedness), while Florida has just completed its first El Nino Awareness week. This year, I've beefed up my solar preps, adding a second solar panel, and additional battery capacity (see #NPM26: It's a 12 Volt Life). I've added a battery operated camp shower, a better shortwave radio, and have recently gone through and thrown out long out-of-date canned food from my pantry. None of which guarantees I'll come away unscathed from an emergency, but I firmly believe it greatly increases my chances. While I'm far from a luddite (I love my gadgets), I know that things break. And as a (former) computer programer I know the more complicated a system becomes, the more likely it is to fail and the harder it will be to fix. Given the complexities of our aging infrastructure, it follows that more failures can be expected. Whether due to natural disasters, failed upgrades, `bad actors', or simply bad luck . . . the odds increase a little each day that you will be adversely affected. The question isn't whether another emergency will arise, it is whether you and your family will be ready to deal with it. How you should prepare will depend upon where you live, the likely threats you will face, and logistical, physical, or financial limitations. I'm unlikely to freeze to death here in Florida, but heat-related deaths are relatively common. And while Southern California doesn't worry about hurricanes, they do have a significant seismic threat. How you go about preparing may be different, but your goals are pretty similar. So if the power goes out today - and stays out for a week - do you have? A battery operated NWS Emergency Radio to find out what was going on, and to get vital instructions from emergency officials A decent first-aid kit, so that you can treat injuries Enough non-perishable food and water on hand to feed and hydrate your family (including pets) for the duration A way to provide light when the grid is down. A way to cook safely without electricity A way to purify or filter water A way to handle basic sanitation and waste disposal. A way to stay cool (fans) or warm when the power is out. A small supply of cash to use in case credit/debit machines are not working An emergency plan, including meeting places, emergency out-of-state contact numbers, a disaster buddy, and in case you must evacuate, a bug-out bag Spare supply of essential prescription medicines that you or your family may need A way to entertain yourself, or your kids, during a prolonged blackout A good place to get started is by visiting Ready.gov, or by hitting this link which will serve up a series of my preparedness blogs. While you may go years without needing it, with emergency preparedness it is better to be ready 5 years too soon than 5 minutes too late. title: Development of lipid nanoparticle mRNA vaccines against swine influenza
abstract: Swine influenza A viruses (IAV-S) cause highly contagious respiratory disease in pigs and pose zoonotic risk due to bidirectional transmission between humans and swine. Managing IAV-S, particularly the H1 subtype, in pigs is vital both to prevent interspecies transmission and to protect the swine industry. Lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-encapsulated mRNA vaccines encoding specific viral antigens offer a rapid, adaptable platform well-suited for targeting rapidly evolving influenza strains. Hemagglutinin (HA), the viral protein that initiates infection, is a critical target for vaccination due to its central role in influenza infection and its antigenic diversity. This study aimed to design and generate three mRNA-LNP vaccine candidates encoding distinct HA antigens: a Taiwan porcine H1, a swine-to-human H1, and a consensus H1. We then evaluated the immunogenicity and cross-reactive potential of these candidates in a mouse model. In vivo evaluation demonstrated that the swine-to-human H1 vaccine candidate induced the broadest humoral IgG response across all three HA antigens, whereas the Taiwan porcine H1 candidate elicited the narrowest cross-reactive immunity. Serum derived from mice-immunized with all three candidate vaccines neutralized the Taiwan porcine H1N2 virus to varying degrees. However, neither intramuscular nor intranasal administration induced mucosal immunity. These results suggest while the swine-to-human HA construct shows strong potential for providing broad systemic immunity, the consensus HA construct requires further optimization. An effective swine influenza vaccine strategy may require a combined intramuscular and intranasal approach to ensure comprehensive systemic and mucosal immunity, including the induction of broadly neutralizing antibodies. Further analysis of the cross-protection and cellular immunity elicited by these candidates is necessary.

abstract_original: Swine influenza A viruses (IAV-S) cause highly contagious respiratory disease in pigs and pose zoonotic risk due to bidirectional transmission between humans and swine. Managing IAV-S, particularly the H1 subtype, in pigs is vital both to prevent interspecies transmission and to protect the swine industry. Lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-encapsulated mRNA vaccines encoding specific viral antigens offer a rapid, adaptable platform well-suited for targeting rapidly evolving influenza strains. Hemagglutinin (HA), the viral protein that initiates infection, is a critical target for vaccination due to its central role in influenza infection and its antigenic diversity. This study aimed to design and generate three mRNA-LNP vaccine candidates encoding distinct HA antigens: a Taiwan porcine H1, a swine-to-human H1, and a consensus H1. We then evaluated the immunogenicity and cross-reactive potential of these candidates in a mouse model. In vivo evaluation demonstrated that the swine-to-human H1 vaccine candidate induced the broadest humoral IgG response across all three HA antigens, whereas the Taiwan porcine H1 candidate elicited the narrowest cross-reactive immunity. Serum derived from mice-immunized with all three candidate vaccines neutralized the Taiwan porcine H1N2 virus to varying degrees. However, neither intramuscular nor intranasal administration induced mucosal immunity. These results suggest while the swine-to-human HA construct shows strong potential for providing broad systemic immunity, the consensus HA construct requires further optimization. An effective swine influenza vaccine strategy may require a combined intramuscular and intranasal approach to ensure comprehensive systemic and mucosal immunity, including the induction of broadly neutralizing antibodies. Further analysis of the cross-protection and cellular immunity elicited by these candidates is necessary.
title_original: Development of lipid nanoparticle mRNA vaccines against swine influenza

However, neither intramuscular nor intranasal administration induced mucosal immunity. These results suggest while the swine-to-human HA construct shows strong potential for providing broad systemic immunity, the consensus HA construct requires further optimization. An effective swine influenza vaccine strategy may require a combined intramuscular and intranasal approach to ensure comprehensive systemic and mucosal immunity, including the induction of broadly neutralizing antibodies. Further analysis of the cross-protection and cellular immunity elicited by these candidates is necessary.

title: Targeting TMPRSS2 protects against influenza-associated lung injury by suppressing PAR-2/MMP-9 axis
abstract: Severe acute lung injury (ALI) induced by influenza A virus is characterized by alveolar hyperpermeability, in which matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) is closely associated with extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation and epithelial barrier compromise. However, the host regulatory mechanism involved in virus-associated MMP-9 upregulation remain incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated the potential involvement of the host protease TMPRSS2 and its downstream partner protease-activated receptor-2 (PAR-2) in modulating MMP-9 expression during A/WSN/33(H1N1) infection. Our findings indicate that viral infection is accompanied by TMPRSS2-mediated PAR-2 activation, alongside downstream engagement of the MEK/ERK and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways and enhanced NF-κB activity, correlating with elevated MMP-9 levels. Pharmacological inhibition of TMPRSS2 with Camostat suppressed PAR-2 activation, attenuated downstream kinase phosphorylation in vitro and in vivo, and was associated with reduced MMP-9 production. Importantly, without apparent alterations in pulmonary viral replication kinetics, TMPRSS2 inhibition helped preserve ECM integrity, mitigated transepithelial electrical resistance (TEER) decline, attenuated alveolar vascular leakage, and reduced inflammatory cytokine release and leukocyte infiltration in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid in infected mice. Collectively, these findings suggest that the TMPRSS2/PAR-2 axis may contribute to influenza-associated lung pathology, providing useful insights into host-targeted protease inhibition as a potential strategy to alleviate severe influenza-induced acute lung injury.

abstract_zh: 甲型流感病毒引起的严重急性肺损伤(ALI)以肺泡通透性过高为特征,其中基质金属蛋白酶-9(MMP-9)与细胞外基质(ECM)降解和上皮屏障受损密切相关。然而,涉及病毒相关 MMP-9 上调的 宿主 调节机制仍不完全清楚。在这项研究中,我们研究了 宿主 蛋白酶 TMPRSS2 及其下游伙伴蛋白酶激活受体 2 (PAR-2) 在 A/WSN/33(H1N1) 感染期间调节 MMP-9 表达的潜在参与。我们的研究结果表明,病毒感染伴随着 TMPRSS2 介导的 PAR-2 激活,以及 MEK/ERK 和 PI3K/AKT 信号通路的下游参与以及增强的 NF-κB 活性,与升高的 MMP-9 水平相关。用卡莫司他对 TMPRSS2 进行药理学抑制可抑制 PAR-2 激活,在体外和体内减弱下游激酶磷酸化,并与 MMP-9 产量减少相关。重要的是,在不明显改变肺部病毒复制动力学的情况下,TMPRSS2 抑制有助于保持 ECM 完整性,减轻跨上皮电阻 (TEER) 下降,减弱肺泡血管渗漏,并减少受感染小鼠支气管肺泡灌洗液中炎症细胞因子的释放和白细胞浸润。总的来说,这些发现表明 TMPRSS2/PAR-2 轴可能有助于流感相关的肺部病理学,为 宿主 靶向蛋白酶抑制作为减轻严重流感引起的急性肺损伤的潜在策略提供了有用的见解。
